**Monocultural Biases: Correlated biases in large language models lead to unequal systemic exclusion rates in hiring.** We study ten LLMs, in both base and post-trained versions, used for hiring automation. Post-training improves callback quality for top candidates but makes models more alike in who they reject: systemic exclusion (being rejected by most models an applicant is evaluated by) rises from 5.6% to 17.3%, reaching 12.2-21.7% for individual post-trained models. This emerges largely through age-based discrimination introduced during post-training, with post-trained models 3.6% less likely to call back older applicants.
